sections.heading: Origins
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Qur'an (1).JPG|thumb|left|180px|[[Ronald Bell (musician)|Ronald Bell]] said "Celebration" was inspired by the [[Quran]] (''pictured'').]]
Co-founder [[Ronald Bell (musician)|Ronald Bell]], the group's saxophonist and musical arranger, said "Celebration" was inspired by the [[Quran]]:

{{blockquote|text=I was reading the passage, where [[God in Islam|God]] was creating [[Adam in Islam|Adam]], and the [[Angels in Islam|angels]] were celebrating and singing praises. That inspired me to write the basic chords, the line, 'Everyone around the world, come on, celebration.'<ref>{{cite news|first= Hisham |last= Aidi |title= Did Coltrane say 'Allah Supreme'? |work= [[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]] |date= December 9, 2014 |access-date= February 20, 2019 |url= https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/opinion/2014/12/did-coltrane-say-allah-supreme-201412810939759431.html}}</ref><ref name="Stereogum"></ref>}}

In ''[[The Guardian]]'', [[Alexis Petridis]] stated that Bell liked telling people that "Celebration" was inspired by the Quran but that [[Robert "Kool" Bell]] had a different explanation of the song's origin. "Kool" recalled Ronald was listening to the band's earlier hit "[[Ladies' Night (song)|Ladies' Night]]" (1979) and noticed the lyric "This is your night tonight, come on, let’s all celebrate." Then, Ronald decided to build a song out of that lyric.<ref name="guardian">{{cite news | last = Petridis | first = Alexis | title = Kool & the Gang's Robert Bell: 'When the astronauts went into space, they played Celebration' | work = [[The Guardian]] | date = July 24, 2023 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/music/2023/jul/24/kool-the-gang-robert-bell | access-date = December 9, 2025}}</ref>
sections.text:
thumb|left|180px|[[Ronald Bell (musician)|Ronald Bell said "Celebration" was inspired by the Quran (pictured).]]
Co-founder Ronald Bell, the group's saxophonist and musical arranger, said "Celebration" was inspired by the Quran:

{{blockquote|text=I was reading the passage, where God was creating Adam, and the angels were celebrating and singing praises. That inspired me to write the basic chords, the line, 'Everyone around the world, come on, celebration.'}}

In The Guardian, Alexis Petridis stated that Bell liked telling people that "Celebration" was inspired by the Quran but that Robert "Kool" Bell had a different explanation of the song's origin. "Kool" recalled Ronald was listening to the band's earlier hit "Ladies' Night" (1979) and noticed the lyric "This is your night tonight, come on, let’s all celebrate." Then, Ronald decided to build a song out of that lyric.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Celebration" is in the A{{flat}} [[Mixolydian mode]] in [[Time signature|common time]] and was written as a collaboration by the whole band.<ref name="Sheet">{{cite web|title= Celebration |website= Sheet Music Direct |url= https://www.sheetmusicdirect.us/sheetmusic/1000046439 |access-date= May 23, 2018}}</ref> The song moves at a [[tempo]] of 123 beats per minute.<ref>{{cite web|title= Celebration – Kool & The Gang |website= Spot on Track |access-date= November 15, 2017 |url= http://www.spotontrack.com/track/celebration/25130151 |archive-date= November 15, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171115143553/http://www.spotontrack.com/track/celebration/25130151}}</ref> The group's vocals span from A{{flat}}<sub>3</sub> to E{{flat}}<sub>5</sub>.<ref name="Sheet"/>
sections.text: "Celebration" is in the A{{flat}} Mixolydian mode in common time and was written as a collaboration by the whole band. The song moves at a tempo of 123 beats per minute. The group's vocals span from A{{flat}}<sub>3</sub> to E{{flat}}<sub>5</sub>.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: ''[[Record World]]'' called the song "one big party hook with cool chorus chants & a boss bass",<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=October 11, 1980|page=1|access-date=2023-02-22|title=Hits of the Week|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/80s/80/Record-World-1980-10-11.pdf}}</ref> while ''[[Stereogum]]'' called Taylor's vocals "calmly ecstatic" and described it as a charmingly simple, and thus, fun song due to its lack of subtext.<ref name="Stereogum">{{cite web |author=Breihan |first=Tom |date=20 April 2020 |title=The Number Ones: Kool & The Gang's Celebration |url=https://stereogum.com/2081505/the-number-ones-kool-the-gangs-celebration/columns/the-number-ones |access-date=23 August 2025 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
"Celebration" reached number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart on February 7, 1981, and held that position for two weeks before [[Dolly Parton]]'s "[[9 to 5 (Dolly Parton song)|9 to 5]]" overtook it.<ref name="MD">{{cite book|first= Maury |last= Dean |author-link= Maury Dean |year= 2003 |title= Rock N' Roll Gold Rush |publisher= Algora |isbn= 0-87586-207-1 |page= [https://archive.org/details/rocknrollgoldrus00dean/page/n318 287] |url= https://archive.org/details/rocknrollgoldrus00dean |url-access= limited}}{{Dead link|date=August 2026|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> It remains the band's only ''Billboard'' number one hit.

By late 1980, the song had also reached number one on both the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Dance Club Songs|Dance]] and [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B]] charts. The song was featured heavily on the radio throughout the year. It has since been frequently used in weddings and parties,<ref name="MD"/> and is a popular anthem for sporting events, including serving as the theme song for the [[St. Louis Cardinals]] after winning the [[1982 World Series]]. In 1981, it was commonly played by radio stations in honor of the release of [[Iran hostage crisis|US hostages from captivity in Iran]].<ref>{{cite book|first= Fred |last= Bronson |year= 2003 |title= The Billboard Book of Number One Hits |publisher= Billboard Books |edition= 5th |page= 536 |isbn= 978-0-82307-677-2}}</ref> It was also an international hit, reaching number seven in the [[United Kingdom]] on November 29, 1980, spending 13 weeks in the chart.
sections.text:
"Celebration" reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart on February 7, 1981, and held that position for two weeks before Dolly Parton's "9 to 5" overtook it. It remains the band's only Billboard number one hit.

By late 1980, the song had also reached number one on both the Billboard Dance and R&B charts. The song was featured heavily on the radio throughout the year. It has since been frequently used in weddings and parties, and is a popular anthem for sporting events, including serving as the theme song for the St. Louis Cardinals after winning the 1982 World Series. In 1981, it was commonly played by radio stations in honor of the release of US hostages from captivity in Iran. It was also an international hit, reaching number seven in the United Kingdom on November 29, 1980, spending 13 weeks in the chart.

"Celebration" was covered in 1987 and released as a single by New Zealand-Australian band [[Dragon (band)|Dragon]]. It was released in November that year by [[RCA Records]] as the lead single from the band's ninth studio album, ''[[Bondi Road (album)|Bondi Road]]'' (1989). The song peaked at number 11 on the Australian [[Kent Music Report]].

"Celebration" was covered by Australian singer and songwriter [[Kylie Minogue]], who originally recorded it for her fourth studio album, ''[[Let's Get to It]]'' (1991), but it was not included on the album's release.<ref name="SJ">{{Cite web |title=Ep 76: Did I Say Ti Amo, Last Thing On My Mind, Celebration and Slam Jam |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/au/podcast/ep-76-did-i-say-ti-amo-last-thing-on-my-mind-celebration/id1565879477?i=1000668115968 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-AU}}</ref> It later appeared on her 1992 ''[[Greatest Hits (1992 Kylie Minogue album)|Greatest Hits]]'' album and was released as its second single on 16 November 1992 by [[Mushroom Records|Mushroom]] and [[Pete Waterman Entertainment|PWL International]]. It was produced by Phil Harding and Ian Curnow, and peaked at number 20 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and at number 21 in Australia. "Celebration" has been cited many times as one of Minogue's favorite songs, and it was included on her greatest hits albums ''[[Ultimate Kylie]]'', ''[[The Best of Kylie Minogue]]'', and ''[[Step Back in Time: The Definitive Collection]]''. The techno-rave mix of the track is featured on the ''[[Kylie's Non-Stop History 50+1]]'' album. It was also Minogue's last single with PWL International and [[Stock Aitken Waterman]].<ref name="SJ" />

"Celebration" was covered by Australian singer and songwriter Kylie Minogue, who originally recorded it for her fourth studio album, Let's Get to It (1991), but it was not included on the album's release. It later appeared on her 1992 Greatest Hits album and was released as its second single on 16 November 1992 by Mushroom and PWL International. It was produced by Phil Harding and Ian Curnow, and peaked at number 20 on the UK Singles Chart and at number 21 in Australia. "Celebration" has been cited many times as one of Minogue's favorite songs, and it was included on her greatest hits albums Ultimate Kylie, The Best of Kylie Minogue, and Step Back in Time: The Definitive Collection. The techno-rave mix of the track is featured on the Kylie's Non-Stop History 50+1 album. It was also Minogue's last single with PWL International and Stock Aitken Waterman.
